messages:
maria_cs: FYI customer ticket #9872 — they hit a 400 on /v1/rerank. They sent a nested payload and the API returned a vague 'invalid input' error. Asking for quick triage and repro steps.

devin_api: Can you paste the exact request body + the error from our logs? that will help.

maria_cs: Pasting redacted payload and server log: 
```json
{
  \"query\": { \"text\": \"how to cancel subscription\" },
  \"documents\": [
    {
      \"title\": \"Billing FAQ\",
      \"candidates\": [
        { \"id\": \"c1\", \"snippet\": \"cancel subscription steps\" },
        { \"id\": \"c2\", \"snippet\": \"refund policy\" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
Server error: `400 invalid input: expected \"candidates\" to be array of strings or objects with \"text\" field; got array of objects missing \"text\"`

kai_eng: This is the crux — our rerank endpoint has two flavors in docs and it trips people up: 
- `candidates`: expected to be either ["string text", ...] OR [{"id":"...","text":"..."}, ...]. field name for the text must be `text` (not `snippet`).
- `documents`: is a higher-level object allowed for batch grouping, and it may contain a `passages` array. If you put `candidates` nested under `documents[*]` we currently do *not* flatten that automatically.

olivia_prd: customer put `snippet` inside the candidate objects — that's the mismatch. Their schema looked like our older internal snippet shape. They also sent `query` as `{text:...}` instead of a top-level `query` string which caused extra parsing code paths. we should probably accept `query.text` too or return a clearer error. :thinking_face: 

devin_api: Repro notes for engineers: the code path that validates candidates expects either string or object w/ top-level `text`. If it sees objects w/o `text` we reject with 400. We also only validate top-level `candidates` array — nested candidates under `documents` are ignored and treated as missing, which then leads to an ambiguous downstream error.

kai_eng: Proposed fix options: 
1) Accept `candidates[*].snippet` as alias for `text` for 1 minor version.
2) Return an explicit validation error that includes the JSON path, eg: `invalid: candidates[0].text missing (found candidates[0].snippet)` so support/clients can patch easily.
3) Add a docs example for `documents` vs `candidates` vs `passages` and a small helper snippet in SDKs to normalize legacy payloads.

monitor-bot: Issue created: INF-4721 - rerank: improve validation error for candidate text field and handle nested candidates. (prio=P2)

maria_cs: Repro steps I gave customer (successful when they flattened): 
1) change payload to: 
```json
{
  "query": "how to cancel subscription",
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"c1","text":"cancel subscription steps"},
    {"id":"c2","text":"refund policy"}
  ]
}
```
2) call /v1/rerank -> returns 200 with scores.
They also reported weird scores (some negatives) when they had nested objects — i think our scorer returned default fallback values if parsing failed.

kai_eng: Yep, fallback scoring can create negative or NaN-ish outputs if inputs are malformed; that's risky. I'll push a small change to make validation strict (reject early) and to ensure we never emit NaN — always return explicit error or null scores.

olivia_prd: Can we also add a note in the API reference: "If you pass `documents`, each document may include `passages` which are used only by the document-level reranker; to supply raw candidates use `candidates` at top level." People keep nesting candidates and expecting implicit flattening.

devin_api: I'll take INF-4721 and add server-side patch + clearer error. also filing DOCS-214 for the examples. Assigning to kai_eng for runtime change and olivia_prd for docs.

maria_cs: Thanks — forwarding the workaround to the customer. tagging back here once they confirm. :thumbsup:
